record.paper_title: Computational issues for linear periodic systems: paradigms, algorithms, open problems
record.original_question: For discrete-time linear periodic systems, can one develop an algorithm for Hankel-norm approximation that is numerically reliable and efficient in the periodic setting?

evidence.quote: For discrete-time systems, we mention the lack of algorithms for computing ... Hankel-norm approximation

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time linear periodic system of period K ≥ 1, given by

  x(k+1) = A(k) x(k) + B(k) u(k),
  y(k)   = C(k) x(k) + D(k) u(k),

where A(k), B(k), C(k), D(k) are real matrices that are periodic in k with period K (so A(k+K)=A(k), etc.), and the system is assumed to be uniformly exponentially stable. Such a system has an associated time-varying Hankel operator H mapping past inputs to future outputs, whose induced ℓ²-operator norm is the Hankel norm ‖·‖_H of the system.

Given a target McMillan degree profile {r(k)}_{k=0}^{K-1} that is strictly less than the corresponding state dimension profile, the optimal Hankel-norm approximation problem asks for a stable discrete-time periodic system Ĝ of the prescribed reduced degree profile that minimizes ‖G − Ĝ‖_H, where G is the original periodic system.

Problem. Develop a numerically reliable and computationally efficient algorithm that, given the periodic state-space data {A(k), B(k), C(k), D(k)}_{k=0}^{K-1}, computes such an optimal (or near-optimal) Hankel-norm approximant Ĝ in the periodic setting, with proven backward-stability or comparable numerical reliability guarantees and complexity scaling gracefully in K and the state dimensions.
artifact.status_search_result: Hankel-norm approximation methods for discrete-time periodic systems have been proposed (e.g., approaches based on solving periodic Lyapunov equations and computing balanced periodic realizations), and these provide model-reduction procedures with error bounds. However, a fully numerically reliable and efficient algorithm comparable in maturity to Glover's optimal Hankel-norm approximation for LTI systems does not appear to be definitively established for the general periodic case, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Model Reduction of Linear Discrete-Time Periodic Systems Using Hankel-Norm Approximations
status_evidence.snippet: The balanced periodic system is obtained by solving the Lyapunov equations using recently proposed methods.
status_evidence.claim: Hankel-norm based model reduction procedures for discrete-time periodic systems have been formulated using periodic Lyapunov equations and balancing.

status_evidence.title: All Optimal Hankel-Norm Approximations of Linear Multivariable Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Glover developed the Hankel norm approximation (HNA) algorithm for optimally reducing the system in the Hankel norm.
status_evidence.claim: For the standard LTI case, an optimal Hankel-norm algorithm is well established (Glover); the periodic counterpart is less developed.
